# xshield_open_ports (Data Source)

Listening ports observed on assets, with the review decision and what is enforced.

This is how to see what a template would have to cover before writing one. Each port carries two states: `listen_port_reviewed` is the intent, `listen_port_enforced` is what the firewall is actually running. They differ until a deployment runs.

The two scales are not the same enum. A template port takes `denied`, `allow-intranet`, `allow-any`, `path-restricted` or `on-demand`, whereas the enforced value here can also be `allowed-by-assetpolicy` or `allowed-test-denied`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Which inbound ports a payroll template would have to cover.
data "xshield_open_ports" "payroll" {
  criteria = "application = 'payroll' AND environment = 'prod'"
}

# Ports carrying no decision yet, which a deployment would leave in test.
output "unreviewed" {
  value = [
    for p in data.xshield_open_ports.payroll.ports :
    "${p.asset_name} ${p.listen_port_protocol}/${p.listen_port}"
    if p.listen_port_reviewed == "unreviewed"
  ]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `criteria` (String) Criteria selecting the ports, written against the port scope.

### Optional

- `destination_criteria` (String) Additional criteria narrowing the destination of the observed traffic.
- `max_results` (Number) Stop after this many results. Left unset, every match is read. When a limit truncates the result set, `truncated` is true.
- `source_criteria` (String) Additional criteria narrowing the peer at the far end of the observed traffic.

### Read-Only

- `ports` (Attributes List) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--ports))
- `total` (Number) Total number of ports matching the criteria, as reported by the API.
- `truncated` (Boolean) True when `max_results` stopped the read before the end of the result set.

<a id="nestedatt--ports"></a>
### Nested Schema for `ports`

Read-Only:

- `asset_id` (String)
- `asset_name` (String)
- `id` (String) Port identifier, derived from the port, protocol and direction.
- `internet_path_count` (Number) How many of those paths came from the internet.
- `listen_port` (String) Port number, or a range such as 8000-8100.
- `listen_port_enforced` (String) What the firewall is enforcing for this port today.
- `listen_port_name` (String)
- `listen_port_protocol` (String)
- `listen_port_reviewed` (String) The decision recorded for this port, which is intent rather than enforcement.
- `listen_process_names` (List of String) Processes observed listening on the port.
- `listening_on_public_interface` (Boolean) True when the port is bound to a publicly reachable interface.
- `matched_by_templates` (List of String) Names of the templates whose rules cover this port.
- `path_count` (Number) Observed traffic paths reaching this port.
